commitMessage: test: verify copied Math Standard archives and remaining scope refusals

contribution.summary: Activate bounded package-risk Verification with the original Math physical archive verifier on a received copy, rejecting tampering, version forgery, false first-pass history and all-package overclaims.
contribution.value: RS324 succeeded first-pass under DWF 0.1.72, completing only the three-archive Standard/Expression/Quantities GREEN and readying T2 Verification. RS325 independently copies ten canonical SDK/project/ledger/report/verifier inputs and exactly three immutable physically SHA-pinned nupkg archives to a short disposable working root. It invokes the existing RS322 physical validator against that copied NUGET_LOCAL feed, requires a clean pass, injects and refuses archive tampering, forged Standard version, RS254 first-pass history falsification and an unsupported claim that ten remaining packages are qualified, then revalidates each restored copy and canonical hash. RS323's separate net11.0 locked restore is established by durable evidence, not replayed. Activate T2 Verification only; no global package qualification, migration, publication or guidance upgrade.
debtChanges: RS324 succeeded first-pass and completed the bounded three-package GREEN; the package-risk Verification leaf is ready but not yet started.
RS325 reuses the existing RS322 source and physical archive validator in a separately copied ten-file corpus and three-archive feed, rather than building a duplicate package risk engine.
Copied-only mutations must be refused and exactly restored: changed archive, forged version, RS254 first-pass misreport and erasure of explicit ten-package coverage limits.
Preserve original NuGet archives, production SDK 10.0.401/net10.0/C#14 and DWF guidance 0.26 under the separate BL0028/RS0 consumer upgrade hold.
contribution.nextAction: Once RS325 independently verifies physical and provenance refusals, separately assess T2 Verification and C01 task closure strictly within the three-package evidence; retain other ten library gaps.
